message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I am p3 with $522 and four properties. The opponent is p1, who has a massive empire of browns, oranges, and greens with four houses each, plus cash and a Get Out of Jail Free card. I am on MARVIN_GARDENS.

Marvin Gardens is mortgaged by p1, so no rent is due. I am weighing post-turn actions: trade, mortgage, unmortgage, or end turn. I will skip unmortgaging PARK_PLACE since no houses remain in the bank. I am now mapping the standard Monopoly board positions to assess my next roll.

I have mapped the full Monopoly board. I am on space 29, Marvin Gardens. The opponent ended their turn at the start of this turn, so I have not rolled yet.

I am unsure whether this is the post-roll phase or between turns. I recall ending on Illinois last turn, so I may have moved to Marvin Gardens during p1's turn.

I now see this is a post-turn action decision, not a roll. I likely rolled five spaces from Illinois to land on the mortgaged Marvin Gardens. The bank has zero houses and twelve hotels.

Unmortgaging PARK_PLACE would cost about $193, leaving only $329 in cash. I still cannot build because the bank has no houses. Hotels require four houses first, so unmortgaging would not generate rent until houses return.

I am calculating the opponent's hotel options. Two brown properties could each host a hotel for $50, freeing eight houses. Three orange properties would cost $100 each to hotel, totaling $300. The opponent only has $257, so they might build two hotels and free eight houses.

I am now calculating the rent on Pacific Avenue if I land there with four houses. The rent would be $1,100, which is a major risk. I also noted that the opponent cannot afford to hotel all three green properties.

I mapped the full roll outcomes from Marvin Gardens. Rolling three, four, or six lands on green properties with four houses, costing about $1,100 to $1,200 in rent. Rolling seven hits an unmortgaged railroad for $100. Rolling nine lands on my mortgaged Park Place, so no rent is due. Rolling twelve collects $200 for landing on GO. About 30% of rolls from here are fatal to my cash.

I calculated that mortgaging all my properties would only yield about $385, which is still too little to survive a $1,100 green rent. Unmortgaging Park Place would not improve this. I am now considering trading with p1, but they already hold massive monopolies and do not need my assets to win. My only remaining path to victory is completing a dark blue monopoly with houses before the opponent lands on it.

I am now calculating exact distances from the opponent's current space, Ventnor. Park Place is ten spaces away and Boardwalk is twelve.

I also checked whether trading with p1 could help. They own Indiana and Illinois but lack Virginia, so they cannot complete the red monopoly. They already hold Kentucky, which I own, so no useful exchange exists.

I realized Virginia is purple, so I am blocking the red monopoly. Trading Kentucky to p1 would let them complete reds and build houses, which would be catastrophic for me. Boardwalk and Park Place are my only kill shots and must never be sold. Utilities are not a win condition. I cannot ask p1 to demolish properties. I am now searching for any trade that could give me a property that creates a usable monopoly.

No trade offers any benefit. Mortgaging now would only waste the 10% interest penalty, and I cannot buy unowned properties during post-turn actions. The correct move is end_turn.

I will keep cash liquid and avoid any mortgage, trade, or unmortgage action. I am calculating the exact rent for one house on Boardwalk and Park Place to reassess whether a dark blue monopoly can still be lethal if houses return from hotels.
